lines.text: Here's how the Claude Code team does code review, in under sixty seconds.
With agents writing code, Anthropic's daily changes jumped from twenty-five hundred to over thirty thousand.
Nobody can read all that, so they stack layers, not one gate.
Say you ask Claude to fix a bug. Let's follow the fix through each layer.
Layer one, on your machine: Claude runs the tests, then a second Claude, with fresh eyes, rereads the change.
Layer two, in review: several agents hunt for bugs at once.
Another group votes on each finding, and it's only posted if enough agree it's real.
Layer three: security review and checks. Any open finding blocks the merge.
Layer four: people, scaled by risk. Docs need no approver, normal changes one, the riskiest two.
In three months, merged changes more than doubled, and the rollback rate fell over forty percent.
The AI never approves. It only posts findings.
